intro: Summarize a small data set the way the exam expects: the mean, the median, the range, the sample standard deviation and the standard error. Type each answer, check it, and every step of the working appears.
howItWorksTitle: The formulas, and how answers are checked
howItWorks:
mean x̄ = Σx / n

s = √( Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1) )

SE = s / √n

  • The median is the middle value once the values are sorted (the mean of the two middle values when n is even). The range is largest minus smallest.
  • The standard deviation s measures how spread out the values are. Divide by n − 1 because the data are a sample, not the whole population.
  • The standard error SE measures how precisely the sample mean estimates the true mean. Larger samples give smaller SE.
  • An answer counts when it is within one unit of the last decimal place asked for. For s and SE it may also be within 1%, so rounding the mean on the way does not cost you the point.

explore.about: Tools v2 Explore (docs/tools-v2-bio-descriptive-stats-brief.md). One tray of radish seedlings at day 7, heights in cm (invented), lined up from shortest to tallest. The first 7 heights open (on a narrow phone the first 5: every plant's column is at least 44 px wide, so a narrow tray holds fewer plants); Add a plant sows the next one in the list, Remove one pulls the last one sown (3 plants up to 10 or what the tray holds). Every number is worked out from the plants as drawn, to the 0.1 cm the clipboard lists: mean, median (the mean of the two middle plants when n is even), sample SD (n − 1) and SE = s ÷ √n.
explore.purpose: See why one tall plant moves the mean more than the median

goals.text: Drag one plant past 11 cm. Which moves more, the mean or the median?
Make the SD as small as you can: bring every plant to almost the same height (SD 0.3 cm or less).
Add plants until the tray is full. Watch SE shrink while the SD stays about the same.

explore.refHtml:
The formulas (AP® Biology Equations and Formulas sheet)

x̄ = (1 ÷ n) Σ xᵢ

s = √( Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² ÷ (n − 1) )

SEx̄ = s ÷ √n

  • Mean: the sum of all the values divided by the number of values, n.
  • Median: the middle value, which separates the greater and lesser halves of the data. Sort the values first; with an even n it is the mean of the two middle values (both middle plants light up).
  • Mode: the value that occurs most often. Measured heights rarely repeat, so a small sample often has no mode.
  • Range: the largest value minus the smallest.
  • s is the sample standard deviation: divide by n − 1, not n, because the plants are a sample of all the plants that could be grown this way. SE is how far the sample mean is likely to be from the true mean; it shrinks as n grows.

Why the mean moves more

The mean uses the size of every value: make one plant 6.8 cm taller and the sum grows by 6.8, so the mean grows by 6.8 ÷ n. The median only cares which plant is in the middle once they are lined up, so one extreme plant moves it by one plant at most. The mean is the balance point of the dots on the clipboard: a dot far out pulls it, like a weight far from the pivot. With an outlier, the median describes the typical plant better.

The radishes

The heights are invented, for radish seedlings 7 days after sowing under one lamp. A plant’s height is measured from the soil to where its two heart shaped seed leaves (cotyledons) meet. A very tall, thin seedling is often one that stretched toward the light.
